_meta.indication: Gadavist is a gadolinium-based contrast agent indicated for intravenous use in diagnostic MRI in adults and children (2 years of age and older) to detect and visualize areas with disrupted blood brain barrier (BBB) and/or abnormal vascularity of the central nervous system.

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, crossover study with an active control (ProHance/gadoteridol); each subject underwent unenhanced MRI followed by contrast-enhanced MRI, evaluated by three independent blinded readers.
pivotal_trials.population: Subjects referred for a contrast-enhanced MRI of the CNS based on current symptoms or on results from a previous imaging procedure.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Superiority of combined unenhanced plus Gadovist-enhanced MRI over unenhanced MRI for three visualization endpoints (contrast enhancement, border delineation, internal morphology), and non-inferiority for the number of lesions detected.
pivotal_trials.result: Gadovist provided a statistically significant improvement (p<0.001) for all three visualization endpoints; for the number of lesions detected in Study A (310123), Gadavist and gadoteridol did not meet the prespecified noninferiority margin of -0.35.

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, open-label study identical to Study 310123 except without the active comparator arm; subjects underwent unenhanced MRI followed by Gadovist-enhanced MRI.
pivotal_trials.population: Subjects referred for contrast MRI of the CNS based on symptoms or previous imaging results.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Superiority of combined unenhanced plus Gadovist-enhanced MRI over unenhanced MRI for three visualization endpoints (contrast enhancement, border delineation, internal morphology), and non-inferiority for number of lesions detected.
pivotal_trials.result: Gadovist provided a statistically significant improvement (p<0.001) for all three visualization endpoints; for the number of lesions detected, Study B (310124) met the prespecified noninferiority margin of -0.35 for paired read versus pre-contrast read.

key_safety: Adverse reactions were usually mild to moderate; the most frequent (≥0.5%) were headache (1.5%), nausea (1.2%), injection site reactions (0.6%), dysgeusia (0.5%) and feeling hot (0.5%). The most serious reactions are nephrogenic systemic fibrosis and hypersensitivity/anaphylactoid reactions.
target_moa: Gadavist (gadobutrol) is a paramagnetic macrocyclic contrast agent; when placed in a magnetic field it shortens the T1 and T2 relaxation times, producing signal enhancement in tissues where the contrast agent accumulates.

boxed_warning.content: Boxed warning for Nephrogenic Systemic Fibrosis (NSF): GBCAs increase the risk for NSF among patients with impaired elimination of the drugs; NSF may result in fatal or debilitating fibrosis affecting the skin, muscle and internal organs.

advisory_committee.vote: Presented to the Peripheral and Central Nervous System Advisory Committee on January 21, 2011; the committee voted 16 to 0 to recommend gadobutrol approval, and voted 15 to 1 to support no NSF contraindication in the label.

description.text: Added new indication: Gadavist with MRI to detect the presence and extent of malignant breast disease

citations.quote: This “Prior Approval” supplemental new drug application provides for a new indication: Gadavist is indicated with MRI to detect the presence and extent of malignant breast disease.

description.text: Added detection/visualization of disrupted blood brain barrier and/or abnormal CNS vascularity in adult and pediatric patients including term neonates

citations.quote: This “Prior Approval” supplemental new drug application provides for detection and visualization of areas with disrupted blood brain barrier (BBB) and/or abnormal vascularity of the central nervous system in adult and pediatric patients (including term neonates).

description.text: Added MR angiography evaluation of known or suspected supra-aortic or renal artery disease in adult and pediatric patients including term neonates

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for evaluation of known or suspected supra-aortic or renal artery disease in adult and pediatric patients (including term neonates).

description.text: Added indication for cardiac MRI to assess myocardial perfusion and late gadolinium enhancement in adults with known or suspected coronary artery disease

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for a new indication for use in cardiac MRI (CMRI) to assess myocardial perfusion (stress, rest) and late gadolinium enhancement in adult patients with known or suspected coronary artery disease (CAD).

summary.text: Gadobutrol was approved as a new gadolinium-based contrast agent based on two confirmatory phase 3 studies (310123, 310124) demonstrating enhanced MRI visualization of CNS lesions and anatomy; the application was reviewed by the Peripheral and Central Nervous System Advisory Committee on January 21, 2011, which voted 16 to 0 to recommend approval, and was approved March 14, 2011.

citations.quote: Bayer HealthCare conducted two confirmatory phase 3 studies to support gadobutrol approval, each designed in a manner similar to those supporting the approval of other GBCAs. The study results demonstrated that gadobutrol enhanced MRI visualization of CNS lesions and anatomy.
The committee voted (16 to 0) to recommend gadobutrol approval.

requirement.text: Required pediatric assessment 1743-1: provide additional nonclinical (animal) data from newborn to juvenile animals to support safety of the product in the 0-23 month pediatric age group.

citations.quote: 1743-1 You must provide additional nonclinical (animal) data to support the safety of your product in the 0-23 month pediatric age group. These nonclinical data should be obtained from newborn to juvenile animals that model pediatric patients in this age group.

requirement.text: Required pediatric assessment 1743-2: study patients 0-23 months of age referred for MRI with contrast; at least 40 patients to characterize pharmacokinetics and support efficacy of Gadavist in this age group.

citations.quote: 1743-2. Your study will examine patients 0-23 months of age who are referred for an MRI exam with contrast. A sufficient number of subjects will be studied to adequately characterize the pharmacokinetics of the product in this age group.
